title: `notifications/prompts/list_changed`
description: The notification a server sends when the set of available prompts changes.
question: Does the framework notice when the prompt list changes?
why: Prompts are surfaced directly to users as commands. A stale list means a command menu that offers entries the server has withdrawn.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers publishing this. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.genkit_js: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no handler for `notifications/prompts/list_changed` is registered and there is no change hook; each `getActivePrompts` call lists again, so a caller that re-lists sees the added prompt.
notes.mastra: Mastra 2.2.0 against a 2025-11-25 server: `onListChanged('src', fn)` installs the handler, and it fired and the next list showed the change. But the call itself rejects with `subscriptions/listen needs MCP 2026-07-28`, because it also tries to open a 2026-07-28 stream. Code that awaits the registration sees an error for a hook that works.
notes.crewai: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes.langchain: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: there is no prompt listing API (`load_mcp_prompt` expands one prompt by name), so an added prompt cannot be discovered through the adapter whatever the notification says.
notes.google_adk: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no prompt methods, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes.autogen: AutoGen 0.7.5: The workbench registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification; its `list_prompts` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `on_tools_changed` is the only change hook, and it covers tools only. Nothing hears the prompts notification, but `list_prompts_sync` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. `experimental_listPrompts()` fetches on every call, so the next list shows the added prompt.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: no prompts method and no notification hook, so a prompt-list change has no route to the caller.
notes.semantic_kernel: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the default `message_handler` awaits `load_prompts()` inside the MCP session's receive loop, deadlocking the session until the request times out; the prompt list stays stale.
notes.llamaindex: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes no message handler and closes its session after every call (over stdio it also starts a fresh server process per call), so no session is open to hear `notifications/prompts/list_changed`, and the next `list_prompts` did not show the added prompt.
notes.pi: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `onNotification` would hear `notifications/prompts/list_changed`, but `McpClient` has no prompts method to list the change with.
notes.google_adk_js: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset` has no prompt listing API, so there is nothing to refresh.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so a prompts list_changed notification has nothing to refresh, and no hook hears it.
notes.haystack: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPToolset` has no prompt API, so `notifications/prompts/list_changed` reaches nothing.
notes.smolagents: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes.dspy: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session. No listing means no change to see.
notes.langchain_js: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): there is an `onPromptsListChanged` server option, but with no prompts API there is nothing to relist, so the notification has no route to the application.
notes.beeai: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no prompt listing to refresh; BeeAI converts tools only and has no notification hook.
notes.crewai-native: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler and has no list-changed hook, so `notifications/prompts/list_changed` goes unseen and the next list is whatever the caller asks for again.
notes.google_adk_java: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: The adapter registers no `promptsChangeConsumer` consumer, so nothing tells the agent the list changed. The next `McpToolset.getTools` call (or session `listPrompts`) lists again and shows the change.
notes.koog: Koog 1.3.0-beta: same as resources: no hook, and the next `Client.listPrompts` on the underlying `Client` shows the change.
notes.google_adk_go: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): a `PromptListChangedHandler` on the caller's `*mcp.Client` hears the notification, but mcptoolset lists only tools, so the agent has no prompts list to refresh.
